dinosaurs.label: Dinosaurs
dinosaurs.blurb: Fifty dinosaurs: what to feed them and how to tell them apart
dinosaurs.intro: Meet the dinosaurs! Feed each one what it ate — meat or plants — and know a dinosaur by its special mark.

epochs.label: Time Machine
epochs.blurb: Surprise tasks about time: what came earlier and what came later
epochs.intro: Let’s climb into the time machine! Every time it brings new tasks: put events in order, guess what appeared earlier, and find out when it was. After every task there is a short story.

world_figures.label: Great People of the World
world_figures.intro: Meet the people who changed the world: scientists, artists and explorers. On every step there are new people, and the ones you know come back so that you don’t forget them.

ua_figures.label: Great People of Ukraine
ua_figures.intro: Ukraine has many great people: poets, princes, scientists and astronauts. Find out what they are famous for!

inventions.label: Great Inventions of the World
inventions.intro: The light bulb, the telephone, the airplane — someone once thought up each of them for the very first time. Find the inventor!

ua_inventions.label: Great Inventions of Ukraine
ua_inventions.intro: The helicopter, the kerosene lamp, the biggest airplane in the world — all of these were thought up in Ukraine. Meet these inventions!

pl_figures.label: Great People of Poland
pl_figures.blurb: Kings, scientists and artists of Poland
pl_figures.intro: Poland has many great people: kings and knights, scientists, poets and musicians. Find out what they are famous for!

pl_inventions.label: Great Inventions of Poland
pl_inventions.intro: The kerosene lamp, vitamins, the walkie-talkie, the Moon rover — Poles thought up all of these. Find the inventor!

SEQUENCES: Ages of history|Stone Age|Ancient Egypt|Middle Ages|Today|First people lived in caves, then they built pyramids, after that castles, and now skyscrapers.

How people traveled|Horse|Steam locomotive|Automobile|Rocket|For thousands of years the horse was the fastest. The steam locomotive appeared only two hundred years ago, and people reached space later still.

How people wrote down their thoughts|Drawings on rocks|Scroll|Printed book|Computer|The oldest cave drawings are tens of thousands of years old. People learned to print books about six hundred years ago.
Where people lived|Cave|Hut|Castle|Apartment building|People’s homes grew stronger and taller all the time: from a cave to a building a hundred stories high.
How people made light at night|Campfire|Candle|Kerosene lamp|Light bulb|The kerosene lamp was invented in Lviv in 1853, and the electric light bulb lit up a quarter of a century after that.
The history of Ukraine|Trypillians|Kyivan Rus|Cossacks|Independent Ukraine|The Trypillians made painted pots more than five thousand years ago, and Ukraine became independent in 1991.
How people passed on news|Letter|Telephone|Television|Smartphone|A letter took weeks. Today a message flies around the Earth faster than you can blink.

How people rose into the sky|Hot-air balloon|Airplane|Helicopter|Spaceship|The first to rise into the sky, in a hot-air balloon, were the Montgolfier brothers. The airplane took off a hundred and twenty years after that.
How people listened to music|Radio|Cassette|Compact disc|Music on a phone|Once, to hear a song, you had to wait for it on the radio. Now millions of songs fit in a pocket.
What people counted with|Fingers|Abacus|Calculator|Computer|We count in tens because we have ten fingers — they are the oldest “counting machine.”
What ships were like|Dugout boat|Sailing ship|Steamship|Cruise liner|The first boats were hollowed out of a whole tree trunk. A liner of today is a floating city for several thousand people.
Tools|Stone hand ax|Bronze ax|Iron hammer|Robot|Whole ages are named after what tools were made of: the Stone Age, the Bronze Age, the Iron Age.
How people told the time|Sundial|Hourglass|Mechanical clock|Digital watch|A sundial does not work at night or in cloudy weather, so people kept thinking up clocks that were more and more exact.
What money was like|Shells|Coins|Paper money|Bank card|People once paid with shells, salt and furs. The first coins were struck more than two and a half thousand years ago.
How people kept pictures|Painting|Camera|Movie camera|Phone camera|For the first photograph in the world you had to wait several hours. Now a picture is ready in an instant.
Who lived on Earth|Dinosaurs|Mammoths|Pyramid builders|Knights|Dinosaurs vanished millions of years before people appeared. But the mammoths were seen by early people with their own eyes.

Events in the history of Kyiv|The founding of Kyiv|Saint Sophia Cathedral|Kyiv-Mohyla Academy|The Kyiv subway|The story goes that Kyiv was founded by the brothers Kyi, Shchek and Khoryv and their sister Lybid. The subway in the city opened in 1960.

The conquest of space|The first satellite|The first person in space|People on the Moon|The International Space Station|Only twelve years passed from the first satellite to a person’s steps on the Moon.
How people got their food|Hunting and gathering|The first fields|A plow with oxen|Tractor|When people learned to grow grain, they no longer had to wander — and so villages and towns appeared.
What roads were like|Footpath|Cobblestones|Railroad|Highway|The ancient Romans paved their roads with stone so well that you can still walk along some of them today.
How doctors learned to heal|Healing herbs|Microscope|Vaccine|X-ray|Through the microscope people first saw germs, and later they learned to protect themselves from them with vaccines.
Machines that count|Abacus|A computer that fills a room|Laptop|Smartphone|The first computers filled a whole room and counted more slowly than your phone.

The best-known buildings in the world|The Pyramids of Giza|The Parthenon|The Colosseum|The Eiffel Tower|The pyramids are more than four and a half thousand years old. When the Colosseum was being built, they were already very old.

Well-known Ukrainian books|“The Tale of Bygone Years”|Kotliarevsky’s “Eneida”|Shevchenko’s “Kobzar”|“The Forest Song”|“The Tale of Bygone Years” was written by the chronicler Nestor nine hundred years ago. “Kobzar” came out in 1840.

The history of sports contests|Olympic Games in Greece|Knights’ tournaments|The modern Olympic Games|Sports on television|In Ancient Greece wars were stopped for the time of the Olympic Games. The modern games were brought back in 1896.
Where people got the power for machines|Fire|Windmill|Steam engine|Solar panels|The steam engine changed the world: factories, trains and steamships appeared.
What people wrote with|Goose quill|Fountain pen|Ballpoint pen|Keyboard|People wrote with goose quills for more than a thousand years. The ballpoint pen was thought up less than a hundred years ago.

Great journeys|Columbus sails to America|Magellan’s voyage around the world|The climbing of Everest|The flight to the Moon|Magellan’s ships were the first to sail around the whole Earth — it took three years.
EARLIER: Bicycle|Automobile|The first bicycle had no pedals — riders pushed off the ground with their feet. The automobile appeared seventy years later.
Telephone|Radio|Alexander Bell patented the telephone in 1876, and radio began to work about twenty years later.
Steam locomotive|Airplane|Steam locomotives had been carrying people for a hundred years when the Wright brothers first took off in an airplane in 1903.
Printed book|Newspaper|First Gutenberg learned to print books, and newspapers began to come out a century and a half later.
Candle|Light bulb|People made light with candles for thousands of years, and the light bulb appeared only about a hundred and fifty years ago.
Castles|Skyscrapers|Castles were built of stone for protection. Skyscrapers became possible when the steel frame and the elevator were invented.
Dinosaurs|People|Dinosaurs vanished sixty-six million years ago — long before the first person.
Abacus|Calculator|People counted on the abacus back in ancient times, and the pocket calculator appeared about fifty years ago.
Photography|Movies|The first photograph was taken in 1826. A movie is many photographs that quickly follow one another.
Television|Home computer|Televisions appeared in homes in the middle of the twentieth century, and computers a few decades later.
The internet|Smartphone|At first the internet joined only big computers. Smartphones appeared much later.
Sailing ship|Steamship|Sailing ships depended on the wind. A steamship could sail anywhere in any weather.
Hot-air balloon|Airplane|People rose into the sky in a hot-air balloon in 1783 — a hundred and twenty years before the first airplane.
Telescope|Space rocket|First people looked at the stars through a telescope for four hundred years, and only then did they fly toward them.
Coins|Paper money|Coins are heavy, so in China paper money was thought up — it is easier to carry.
Goose quill|Ballpoint pen|A quill had to be dipped in ink all the time. A ballpoint pen writes by itself.
The Pyramids|The Colosseum|When the Romans were building the Colosseum, the pyramids of Egypt were already more than two and a half thousand years old.
The Great Wall of China|The Eiffel Tower|The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries. The Eiffel Tower went up in two years — in 1889.
Wheel|Bicycle|The wheel was thought up more than five thousand years ago. Without it there would be no carts, no bicycles and no automobiles.
Fire|Wheel|People used fire for hundreds of thousands of years, and the wheel is a much younger invention.
Soccer|Basketball|The rules of soccer were written down in England in 1863. Basketball was thought up by a gym teacher in 1891.
Refrigerator|Microwave oven|Food used to be kept in cellars with ice. The microwave oven was invented by accident — a chocolate bar melted in an engineer’s pocket.
Piano|Electric guitar|The piano was created in Italy around 1700. The electric guitar is not yet a hundred years old.
Subway|Helicopter|The first subway opened in London in 1863 — its trains were pulled by steam locomotives.
The first satellite|People on the Moon|The satellite was launched in 1957, and people set foot on the Moon in 1969.
Postage stamp|Email|The first postage stamp came out in 1840. The first email was sent in 1971.
Kyivan Rus|The Zaporozhian Sich|Kyivan Rus existed more than a thousand years ago. The Cossacks appeared several centuries later.
Papyrus|Paper|The Egyptians wrote on papyrus made of reeds. Paper was invented in China almost two thousand years ago.
Eyeglasses|Telescope|Eyeglasses were thought up in Italy more than seven hundred years ago. Later a telescope was put together from the same kind of lenses.
Tower clock|Wristwatch|The first mechanical clocks were huge and stood on towers. Wristwatches appeared much later.
Violin|Piano|The violin was created by Italian masters five hundred years ago. The piano is two centuries younger.
Ancient Greece|The Middle Ages|The ancient Greeks thought up the theater and the Olympic Games. Knights and castles appeared more than a thousand years later.

ITEMS: A mammoth hunt|A mammoth gave early people meat, hides for clothes and bones for building.
The first campfire|Fire gave warmth, scared off wild animals and helped to cook food.
Stone hand ax|The hand ax is one of the first tools: people cut, scraped and chopped with it.
Drawings in a cave|On the walls of caves early people drew bulls, horses and deer with ocher and charcoal.
Bow and arrows|With a bow you could hunt from far away — it was a great invention.
A needle of bone|With a bone needle people sewed warm clothes out of hides.
The building of the pyramids|The pyramids are the tombs of the pharaohs. The biggest is built of more than two million blocks of stone.
A Greek temple|The ancient Greeks built temples of white marble in honor of their gods.
Gladiators in the Colosseum|The Colosseum in Rome held fifty thousand people.
A papyrus scroll|Papyrus was made from the stems of a reed that grew on the banks of the Nile.
Amphora|In amphoras the Greeks and Romans carried oil, grain and wine.
Pharaoh|A pharaoh was a ruler of Ancient Egypt. He was thought to be the son of the sun god.
The first Olympic Games|The first games had only one contest — a race of one stade, which is about two hundred meters.
A knight’s castle|A castle was surrounded by a moat of water and thick walls, so that enemies could not get in.
A knight in armor|A knight’s armor weighed as much as a seven-year-old child — more than twenty kilograms.
Prince Yaroslav the Wise|Yaroslav the Wise ruled in Kyiv a thousand years ago and founded the first library in Rus.
Saint Sophia Cathedral|Saint Sophia Cathedral in Kyiv was built under Yaroslav the Wise. It still stands today.
A book copied by hand|A monk spent many months copying one book with a quill, so books cost a great deal.
Vikings in their boats|In their long boats, called longships, the Vikings sailed even as far as America.
A flight into space|The first person flew into space in 1961.
Smartphone|Smartphones appeared only a short while ago — about twenty years ago.
Passenger airplane|Today an airplane crosses the ocean in a few hours. Columbus sailed across it for more than two months.
Computer|Computers appeared in the twentieth century, and at first they filled a whole room.
Subway|The subway carries people under the ground, so as not to get in the way of cars on the streets.
Robot|Robots put automobiles together, explore Mars and even clean the house.
WHEN: When did the dinosaurs vanish?|66 million years ago|1000 years ago|100 years ago|A huge asteroid struck the Earth, and the climate changed sharply. The descendants of the dinosaurs are the birds!
When were the pyramids of Egypt built?|More than 4000 years ago|400 years ago|40 years ago|The pyramids are so old that even for the ancient Greeks they were ancient.
When did Columbus reach America?|More than 500 years ago|50 years ago|5000 years ago|Columbus was looking for a way to India, and came upon lands that Europe did not know about.
When did a person first fly into space?|More than 60 years ago|600 years ago|6000 years ago|The first flight lasted one hundred and eight minutes — one trip around the Earth.
When did Ukraine become independent?|In 1991|In 1891|In 1791|Ukraine’s Independence Day is celebrated on August 24.
When did Yaroslav the Wise rule in Kyiv?|About 1000 years ago|100 years ago|10,000 years ago|Under Yaroslav the Wise, Kyiv was one of the biggest cities of Europe.
When did the first airplane take off?|More than 120 years ago|12 years ago|1200 years ago|The Wright brothers’ first flight lasted only twelve seconds.
When did Gutenberg begin to print books?|Almost 600 years ago|60 years ago|6000 years ago|Thanks to the printing press books became cheaper, and many people learned to read.
When did people first set foot on the Moon?|In 1969|In 1869|In 2019|The astronaut Neil Armstrong said: “That’s one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.”

When did the Cossacks found the Zaporozhian Sich?|About 500 years ago|50 years ago|5000 years ago|The Sich was a fortress on the islands of the Dnipro, where the Cossacks chose their hetman themselves.
When did the Trypillians live?|More than 5000 years ago|500 years ago|50 years ago|The Trypillians lived on the lands of Ukraine in big settlements and painted their pots with patterns.
When were the first Olympic Games held?|About 2800 years ago|280 years ago|28 years ago|The winner was given a wreath of olive branches.
When was the Eiffel Tower built?|More than 130 years ago|13 years ago|1300 years ago|The tower was put up for a world’s fair. At first the people of Paris did not like it!
When did the first computers appear?|About 80 years ago|8 years ago|800 years ago|One of the first computers weighed as much as five elephants.
When did people think up the wheel?|More than 5000 years ago|500 years ago|50 years ago|The very first wheels were solid wooden disks, without spokes.
